'''2-1B/DRX''' was a [[2-1B surgical droid/Legends|2-1B surgical droid]] model that was utilized at the [[Emperor Palpatine Surgical Reconstruction Center|EmPal SuRecon]] center. It was utilized in an attempt to reconstruct [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] after the latter sustained [[Mou kei/Legends|severe injuries]] in his [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|duel]] on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], and was responsible for the development of [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|Darth Vader's life-support armor]]. It was eventually destroyed when Vader, in a [[Force scream/Legends|fit of rage and sorrow]], used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to crush everything within the vicinity of the reconstruction center upon learning of not only his failure to prevent his wife, [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé's]] death, but also being directly responsible for it.

==Personality and traits==
2-1B's personality was best summed up as being quite unpleasant: The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] frequently made several sarcastic remarks at the expense of his patients. A notable instance of this is when he admits in his log on the reconstruction effort for [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] that he deliberately did not give reconstructive cosmetic surgery for Darth Vader's face specifically because "It's not like anyone's ever going to see Vader with Vader's mask off."

==Behind the scenes==
The droid was first seen in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], where it was among the medical droids reconstructing Darth Vader after his injuries on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], as well as being destroyed in the [[Force scream/Legends|aftermath]] from Vader's fury and sorrow.

His character was elaborated on in [[Daniel Wallace]]'s book ''[[Star Wars: Darth Vader: A 3-D Reconstruction Log]]'' as one of the in-universe narrators for the book. Partially in order to not make the book seem like another boring log, Wallace wrote the droid to be an unbearable snarker throughout the procedure, although several of his lines ended up cut in the final release. According to his blog, the snarkiness, in addition to piquing the reader's interest, was also intended to have the readers not feel sorry for him when he ended up destroyed by Darth Vader as in the movie. He also based the character's personality on how [[Scott Chernoff]] wrote the 2-1B droids in the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' column Ask Two-OneBee.
